The main takeaway from our work is that
the A and B band structures of LPS are not only important for the recognition by the host immune system but are also important for the uptake and toxicity of antibiotics.
gentamicin binding to the outer membrane is not a simple process but rather one which is dependent on the LPS composition of the bacterial cell surface.
